sum: A gut bacterium linked with better metabolism. Sold as a "next-generation" probiotic.
b: One small study with pasteurised bacteria
w: Generally safe in studies. Caution if your immune system is suppressed.

sum: Dried liver in capsules, a source of vitamin A, B12, iron and copper.
f: Check the vitamin A per dose
w: A lot of vitamin A: avoid in pregnancy and with other vitamin A supplements. Avoid with haemochromatosis, thalassaemia and Wilson's disease.

sum: An orange pigment the body turns into vitamin A as needed.
b: A safe source of vitamin A from food
f: Supplements do not prevent cancer or heart disease
fd: Carrot, sweet potato, pumpkin, spinach, apricot
w: Supplements increase lung cancer in smokers and people exposed to asbestos (ATBC and CARET trials). High intake harmlessly turns the skin yellow.

sum: A fungus that grows on birch trees. Drunk as a tea or extract.
b: Lab studies only, not in humans
w: Very high in oxalates: kidney damage has been reported with long-term use. Caution with anticoagulants and diabetes medicines.

sum: The green pigment of plants. Supplements contain chlorophyllin, a semi-synthetic form.
w: Green stools and tongue. May increase sensitivity to the sun.

sum: Garlic supplements, usually aged garlic extract or powder.
b: Small drop in blood pressure in hypertension
w: Increases bleeding risk with anticoagulants and before surgery. Reduces the effect of HIV medicines. Garlic breath.

sum: An essential amino acid. Sold mainly for cold sores.
b: Conflicting small studies, perhaps only at 3 g/day or more
w: Generally safe. Avoid with kidney disease. Antiviral medicines are the proven treatment for cold sores.

sum: A herb with soft, hairy leaves, drunk as a tea for coughs.
b: Ear infection pain, in drops with other herbs
w: The fine hairs irritate the throat if not strained well. No ear drops if the eardrum may be perforated.

sum: The leaves and the root are used for different purposes.
b: Urinary symptoms in benign prostate enlargement (root)
fd: Cooked nettles in pies and soups
w: May affect blood sugar, blood pressure, lithium and anticoagulants. Avoid in pregnancy.

sum: Protein from pea, rice or soy, for people who do not eat dairy.
b: Muscle mass with training, similar to whey at an adequate dose
Meeting protein needs on a vegan diet
f: Together they provide all essential amino acids
w: Choose products certified for heavy metals. Caution with kidney disease.

sum: A red seaweed sold as a gel or capsules, often marketed as "nature's multivitamin".
w: Too much iodine can upset the thyroid. Possible heavy metals. Caution with Hashimoto's and in pregnancy.

sum: A resin-like substance from Himalayan rocks, rich in fulvic acid.
f: Only standardised and tested for metals
w: RISK of heavy metals (lead, arsenic) in unprocessed products. Avoid in pregnancy, gout and haemochromatosis.
